title: Policy & Procedure for emergency care including Medico-Legal Case (MLC) care. Protocols for five common emergency conditions including adult and pediatric patient
html:
POLICY & PROCEDURE FOR EMERGENCY CARE:

1. POLICY:

Any emergency Patients other than Scope of hospital services are not admitted in the hospital.

2. PURPOSE:

  • To provide immediate treatment for all life threatening, emergencies.

3. SCOPE: Patients that require emergency care.

4. RESPONSIBILITY:

Medical officer, Nursing Staff.

5. DISTRIBUTION:

Emergency Department/ Casualty.

6. PROCEDURE:

  • Emergency care shall be provided by Hospital on 24 X 7 bases.
  • On arrival at the hospital, the nurse receives the patient; assess the general condition, checks vital signs.
  • The MO clinically examines the patient, takes history and gives necessary initial treatment to stabilize their condition.
  • If the patient needs admission, MO will inform the consultant on call of that concern specialty.
  • The MO explains to the next of kin about the need for admission, possible diagnosis.
  • If the patient requires any urgent radiology / pathology investigation the needful is done before shifting the patient to ward.
  • Any such investigation done at emergency is documented in patient’s file and informed to the ward to avoid replication.
  • The relatives are directed to the admission counter to complete the admission formalities.
  • The nurse/ ward boy will hand over in detail about the patient-treatment given, investigations are done, samples taken and the list of consumables and/ injections administered, as patient data in admission form.
  • If the nature of the injury is not very serious and does not require admission then after initial treatment the patient is discharged.
  • If the patient needs admission but the patient/ NOK refuses then the MO explains the condition of the patient and risk involvement while shifting. If the patient’s NOK still refuses, then patient is discharged after giving basic life support.
  • For all patients attending to the emergency, the relevant data is documented in emergency patient register. The treatment given to patient is recorded in the treatment sheet for emergency.

6.1 Procedure of handling unidentified & unconscious patient:

(These patients are usually brought in by passers-by, sometimes by police or Public services like Fire Service etc.)

  • The patient shall be received in the emergency department and general procedures towards investigations and stabilization commenced.
  • The state of anonymity does not preclude with holding of investigations or treatment in any way what so ever.
  • Under the purview of the duty doctor his belongings should be taken out one by one, documented and searched for any type of ID, phone numbers, address, visiting cards etc. (quite often patients wallet may be robbed and hence have no personal effects like purses, wallets etc.) Hence, careful documentation of the patients belonging is a must.
  • All items removed shall be documented and selected in plastic bags, with the label bearing the/ date, time and ID marks of the patient Name of the Patient will be labeled as anonymous.
  • Neighboring police stations is intimated if the case is MLC and protocol for emergency is followed (if patient is admitted to our hospital).
  • The patient can be transferred to a facility of his/her choice on request with the entire treatment summary but only after the patient is stabilized.
  • When a patient on regaining consciousness or if his relatives or attainder request discharge for any reason, the duty doctor will reassess the case. If the patient’s condition does not warrant discharge, he/she can be allowed to go only signing on the refusal form.
  • Clearing of dues in the above case shall be as per hospital policy.

6.2 Emergency functional Procedure: Evaluate the patient – A. Stable Patient

B. Unstable Patient

A.Stable Patient –

  • Treatment given as per requirement:
  • Prescribe medicine.
  • Minor procedure if needed.
  • Investigations may be advised.
  • Advised indoor admission if required. Patient’s NOK is to the admission counter.
  • Unstable Patient –
  • If patient is unstable & serious the MO applies basic life supports with additional measures like bandages, stitches etc.
  • Contact intensive care unit staffs, briefing them the history, the seriousness of the case as well as to make arrangements for receiving them.
  • Mean while patient’s NOK is sent to the admission counter for the admission formalities.
  • Patient is then sent to the ICU irrespective of the fact that admission procedure is completed or not.

POLICY & PROCEDURE FOR HANDLING OF MEDICO LEGAL CASES:

1. POLICY:

Any patient seeking emergency medical services shall be screened & first aid care to be provided if required. Doctor on duty shall decide whether a case is a medico legal one. All MLC shall be notified to the police as per Policy.

2. PURPOSE: To ensure proper handling of medico legal cases.

3. SCOPE: All cases as per the MLC list are given below.

4. RESPONSIBILITIES:

Emergency medical officer, Emergency Staff, Nurse, Front office.

5. DISTRIBUTION:

Front office, Emergency department, Nursing Administration.

6. PROCEDURE:

  • Clear entry of Name, Age, Sex and the date & Time of arrival entered in the Emergency Register and in the emergency register separately.
  • The MO and nurse should give emergency first aid/ takes resuscitative measures to stabilize the patient and take detailed history of the accident/ incident from the patient / NOK / witness and document it.
  • If the patient has been brought in by witness, the nurse/ MO establish the identity of the patient, notes down date and time when the patient has been brought in, name and address and telephone numbers of at least two witnesses and make every effort to contact the next of kin of the patient.
  • The MO should decide if the patient needs admission or can be treated as an outpatient.
  • The patient who is being admitted, the emergency assessment form is filled or those patient not being admitted, Treatment sheet for emergency are filled. MLC stamp is given on the assessment form by emergency staff in only for admitted cases.
  • Police intimation form is filled by MO in TWO copies (one original & one carbon copy). Both the copies are sent to Police Station. The original copy is kept by the police and the other copy is taken back with the received stamp from the police station.
  • The signature of the police officer receiving the form should be obtained with date and time.
  • The patient is sent to the ward/ICU with the nurse /ward boy and doctor if required.
  • The patient’s NOK are directed to the admission counter to complete the formalities.
  • All MLC cases are recorded in emergency register and master MLC register.
  • In case the patient expires after arrival, be it in Emergency itself or after transfer to the ward, immaterial of the time lapse since arrival. the following procedures should be adhered to viz.:
  • Second Intimation to the Police Station should be dispatched immediately.
  • The Death Summary should not be handed over to the next of kin but to the police.
  • The Body should NOT be handed over to the next of kin but ONLY TO THE POLICE who will arrange for post – mortem.
    • Directive to an MO to appear in the court should be received ONLY by the concerned MO or may be received by the HR Department. The MO or the HR Manager when receiving the summons should clarify the name of the patient treated in the Hospital to whom that case or hearing pertains.
    • The safety of the patient especially in case of assault or foul-play becomes an added point of concern to the Emergency and Security Staff. The necessity to take precautionary steps to safeguard the patient from further injury even if it be just verbal from any third party. Need not be overemphasized.
    • If a case expires in the Emergency soon after arrival, the Death Summary should contain details of any new wounds inflicted in course of the treatment like:
  • Cut downs.
  • Exploratory extensions of existing wounds.
  • I.V. Punctures and their sites and details of other invasive procedures.
  • External Cardiac Massage.
  • This holds good for those cases that die subsequent to an Emergency Operative Procedure also. This will help in clarifying as to which wounds are Iatrogenic.
  • If a patient or his relatives or both parties concerned request or demand that their case is not to be intimated to the police, it is to be borne in mind that the Medical Officers is not an arbiter. Even if the concerned NOK decide to come to a compromise and both are willing to sign to that effect it is not the duty of the Medical Officer to bear witness to such an agreement, it is left for the Police.
  • Any Compromise or withdrawals of complaints should be done through a law enforcement officer ONLY. Hence, intimating to the police of any case that has been decided to be treated as a MLC becomes mandatory.

6.1 Brought in dead cases:

If the patient has been brought dead, the MO explains to next of kin that the HOSPITAL not accept any brought dead cases / not issue death certificate against any brought dead cases.

POLICY & PROCEDURE FOR TRIAGE OF PATIENT:

1. POLICY:

Triage shall be initiated whenever faced with a situation of mass casualties. All healthcare personnel especially those working in the emergency department should be aware of the importance for triage of the patients.

2. PURPOSE:

If faced with large number of casualties needs to prioritise management

  • Aim is to 'do the best for the most'
  • Triage is the sorting of casualties by priority of treatment
  • Performed by a 'Triage officer'(who is nominated by EMO) who assesses casualties without giving treatment
  • Divides patients into categories
  • Casualties may be given coloured triage label.

3. SCOPE:

All Patients of Mass Casualties.

4. RESPONSIBILITIES:

RMO, Nurse.

5. DISTRIBUTION:

RMO, Nursing.

6. PROCEDURE:

The procedure for triage of the patients is followed only when there is a mass casualty or a group of more than 10 patients coming to the emergency department at the same time.

The nurse on duty shall function as a triage nurse and shall initiate the triage activity when required. She will also inform other staff about occurrence of mass casualties.

6.1 Triage categories:

CategoryDefinitionColourTreatmentExample
P1 (First priority)Life-threateningRedImmediateTension pneumothorax
P2(Second priority)UrgentYellowUrgentFractured femur
P3 (Third priority)MinorGreenDelayedSprained ankle
P4 (Forth priority)DeadBlack

6.2 Methods of triage:

Triage can be performed rapidly by assessing-

  • Airway.
  • Response to verbal command.
  • Respiratory rate.
  • Circulation rate: Pulse rate or capillary return.
  • Pupillary reaction.

6.3 Scene assessment:

  • Recognize environmental hazards to rescuers, secure area for treatment.
  • Recognize hazard for patient, protect from further injury.
  • Identify number of patients, initiate triage if appropriate.
  • Observe position of patient, mechanism of injury and surroundings.
  • Identify yourself.
  • Contact dispatch if hospital resources require mobilization, asks for back up if needed.

6.4 Color Code:

Red:

First priority- Immediate, life threatening shock or hypoxia is present , but patient can be stabilized and if given immediate care shall probably survive .

Yellow:

Second priority- Urgent, injuries have systemic implication or effects, but patient is not yet in life threatening, patients seems able to withstand 45 to 60 mins, give appropriate care .

Green:

Third priority- Delayed, injuries are localized and without immediate systemic implications , with a minimum of care, patient does not deteriorate for hours.

Black:

Dead, no distinction can be made between clinical and biological death in a mass casualty incident, and any unresponsive patient who has no spontaneous ventilation or circulation is classified as death.

Protocols for five common emergency conditions including adult and paediatric patient

1. Cardiac Arrest

Adult Protocol (ACLS)

  • Check responsiveness & breathing
  • Call for help + activate emergency response
  • Start CPR immediately
    • Compression rate: 100–120/min
    • Depth: 5–6 cm
  • Attach defibrillator
    • Shock if VF/pulseless VT
  • Medications:
    • Epinephrine every 3–5 min
    • Amiodarone for shockable rhythms
  • Secure airway + give oxygen

Paediatric Protocol (PALS)

  • Compression:
    • Depth: 1/3 chest depth (~4 cm infant, 5 cm child)
  • Ratio:
    • 30:2 (single rescuer)
    • 15:2 (two rescuers)
  • Early respiratory support (kids often arrest due to hypoxia)
  • Use weight-based drug dosing

2. Respiratory Distress / Failure

Adult

  • Assess airway, breathing, oxygen saturation
  • Give high-flow oxygen
  • Consider:
    • Nebulization (salbutamol)
    • Steroids (asthma/COPD)
  • If worsening:
    • Non-invasive ventilation (BiPAP/CPAP)
    • Intubation if needed

Paediatric

  • Look for signs: nasal flaring, grunting, chest indrawing
  • Oxygen via mask or nasal cannula
  • Nebulization (salbutamol ± ipratropium)
  • Avoid tiring the child
  • Early escalation to ventilation if deterioration

3. Anaphylaxis

Adult

  • IM Epinephrine (0.5 mg) immediately
  • Lay patient flat, elevate legs
  • Oxygen + IV fluids
  • Adjuncts:
    • Antihistamines
    • Steroids

Paediatric

  • IM Epinephrine (0.01 mg/kg) (max 0.3 mg)
  • Same supportive care
  • Repeat epinephrine every 5–15 min if needed
  • Continuous monitoring (children deteriorate quickly)

4. Seizures (Status Epilepticus)

Adult

  • Protect airway, prevent injury
  • First-line:
    • IV Lorazepam or Diazepam
  • Second-line:
    • Phenytoin / Levetiracetam
  • Check glucose → treat hypoglycemia

Paediatric

  • ABC stabilization first
  • Benzodiazepines:
    • Midazolam (buccal/intranasal if no IV)
  • If ongoing:
    • Levetiracetam / Phenytoin
  • Check for fever → treat febrile seizures

5. Shock (Hypovolemic / Septic)

Adult

  • Identify type of shock
  • IV access + fluid resuscitation
    • 500–1000 mL bolus (crystalloids)
  • Oxygen therapy
  • If septic:
    • Early antibiotics
  • Vasopressors if not responding

Paediatric

  • Fluid bolus:
    • 20 mL/kg isotonic saline
  • Reassess after each bolus
  • Early antibiotics in sepsis
  • Signs differ:
    • Tachycardia = early sign
    • Hypotension = late (dangerous)
